RCCG TABERNACLE OF PRAISE · ISTANBULDEVELOPMENT 09 / 01

Two directions, developed further

Monochrome studies · complete parish name · light and dark

01 / Shared Rhythm

Gathering space + collective rhythm

Four unequal folded faces hold a shared open space. Their changing heights suggest people responding together in praise.

Developed: The liked primary form is preserved. The name has more breathing room, and a separate tiny-use drawing opens the intervals.

02 / Open Praise

Tabernacle + Praise through negative space

A P-like outer contour holds an open T-shaped interior. The two letters connect the parish name through one compact gesture.

Developed: A shorter, blunter inner terminal replaces the pointed hook. The open interior is adjusted; the T remains a reading to test.

Top symbols share the same actual ink height. Practical lockups below use the same name scale; the denser Open Praise symbol is 7% smaller for visual balance. Working lettering: Instrument Sans, title case.

RCCG TABERNACLE OF PRAISE · ISTANBULDEVELOPMENT 09 / 02

Shared Rhythm

Preserving the form you liked; opening its tiny-use intervals

What it expresses

A sanctuary is suggested by four folded faces around an open forecourt. Their uneven rise and fall brings praise into the same arrangement, without adding a separate music icon.

What changed

The main symbol is unchanged from Review 08. A dedicated 16–20 px candidate narrows the faces and opens the intervals while retaining the small fold shoulder.

Where to be careful

The primary feels more coherent at normal sizes. The compact cut looks more disconnected when enlarged and should stay a tiny-use experiment. At 16 px, the result is still an abstract rhythm.

Meaning still to test

Architecture, a cultural venue or property branding are possible associations. Praise is an abstract cadence; the full name and church context remain important.

This proof board is scaled to fit the page. Use the separate native PNGs for 1:1 pixel checks. Minimum-size rules remain provisional.

RCCG TABERNACLE OF PRAISE · ISTANBULDEVELOPMENT 09 / 03

Open Praise

A calmer interior within the same compact outer silhouette

What it expresses

The outer P and proposed negative T refer to Praise and Tabernacle. The open exit offers a sense of welcome. It is a name-based figure-ground idea, rather than a literal church building or instrument.

What changed

The main outline is the balanced-counter trial shown second in this proof. Its inner hook ends earlier with a blunt terminal, and the negative stem is slightly wider. The level-terminal trial was not taken forward.

Small-use candidate

The compact drawing further widens the negative stem and shortens the tip. At 16–20 px, the silhouette is clearer than the full letter reading. Normal applications retain the primary.

Meaning still to test

The T is inferential and the P may dominate. A publisher, creative studio or luxury identity is another possible association. This refinement does not establish universal letter recognition.

This proof board is scaled to fit the page. Use the separate native PNGs for 1:1 pixel checks. Minimum-size rules remain provisional.

RCCG TABERNACLE OF PRAISE · ISTANBULDEVELOPMENT 09 / 04

Lettering changes the voice

Three provisional approaches, applied to both directions

01 / Open title case — working choice

Readable word shapes and a welcoming tone. Instrument Sans at weight 470 is used in the new development lockups and application studies.

02 / Measured capitals

A more formal, composed voice. The wide setting brings confidence, but can make the parish feel less personal and require more width at small sizes.

03 / Warm serif

Source Serif 4 adds warmth and a literary character. It can also move the identity toward a traditional institution or publisher.

This board deliberately uses the unchanged Review 08 symbols to isolate the lettering comparison. Current refined symbols appear on the other pages.

Font-based, outlined and optically spaced; these are original font glyphs, not a claim of custom-drawn type. The type decision remains open.
